record.paper_title: Open Questions in the Understanding of Strangeness Production in HIC – Experiment Perspective
record.original_question: Across heavy-ion collision energies ranging from sub-threshold beam energies through SPS, RHIC, and LHC energies, what is the full energy dependence of strangeness enhancement, especially for rare multi-strange strange and anti-strange hadrons such as Ξ and Ω, when the enhancement factor is defined by comparing strange-particle yields in nucleus-nucleus collisions with those in proton-proton collisions?

evidence.quote:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In relativistic heavy-ion physics, the strangeness enhancement factor for a strange hadron species $h$ at center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ is defined by
$$E_h(\sqrt{s_{NN}}) \;=\; \frac{1}{\langle N_{\text{part}}\rangle}\,\frac{\big(dN_h/dy\big)_{AA}}{\big(dN_h/dy\big)_{pp}},$$
where $(dN_h/dy)_{AA}$ and $(dN_h/dy)_{pp}$ denote midrapidity yields per event of species $h$ in nucleus–nucleus and proton–proton collisions respectively, and $\langle N_{\text{part}}\rangle$ is the mean number of participating nucleons in the AA collision.

Determine, as a quantitative function of $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ across the full range from sub-threshold beam energies through SPS, RHIC and LHC energies, the behavior of $E_h(\sqrt{s_{NN}})$ for the singly-strange and especially for the multi-strange (anti-)hadrons $h \in \{\Lambda,\bar\Lambda,\Xi^-,\bar\Xi^+,\Omega^-,\bar\Omega^+\}$. In particular, characterize the magnitude, monotonicity, and any non-monotonic structure of the enhancement for the doubly- and triply-strange species $\Xi$ and $\Omega$ (and their antiparticles) as a function of collision energy, and explain the underlying mechanism (e.g. canonical suppression of strangeness phase space, transition to a grand-canonical regime, or quark–gluon plasma formation) that governs this energy dependence.
artifact.status_search_result: The energy dependence of strangeness enhancement, especially for multi-strange Ξ and Ω hadrons, remains an active experimental and theoretical research topic. While individual measurements at SPS, RHIC and LHC show that enhancement grows with strangeness content and decreases with energy (consistent with canonical suppression at lower energies), a unified quantitative description across all energies is still under investigation, with new measurements (e.g. ALICE pp high-multiplicity, NA61/SHINE, RHIC BES) continuing to refine the picture.

status_evidence.title: Strangeness enhancement and energy dependence in heavy ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Relative enhancement of strange particle yields from p–p/p–A to A–A increases with decreasing energy; at √s=8.7 GeV enhancements of Ω, Ξ, Λ are ~100, 20, 3.
status_evidence.claim: The energy dependence of multi-strange enhancement is complicated and remains a subject of ongoing study.

status_evidence.title: Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity pp collisions
status_evidence.snippet: ALICE first observation of strangeness enhancement in pp collisions, complicating the simple AA/pp baseline picture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results indicate the pp baseline itself depends on multiplicity, so the energy dependence is still being characterized.

status_evidence.title: Strangeness production in O+O collisions at √sNN=7 TeV using various model approaches
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) modelling work continues to address strangeness production across collision energies and systems.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent literature shows the question is still open.
